data.command: I need to find all files modified in the last 24 hours on this system

data.text:
You can use the `find` command to achieve this. I'm running Ubuntu 22.04.3 LTS with kernel 5.15.0-91.

To find all files modified in the last 24 hours, I'll use the `-mtime` option with the `-ls` action. The `-mtime` option takes a numeric value that represents the number of 24-hour periods since the file was last modified. Since we want files modified in the last 24 hours, we can use `-mtime 0`, which refers to files modified within the last 24 hours.

Here's the command:
```bash
find / -mtime 0 -ls
```
This will search the entire filesystem, starting from the root directory `/`. The `-ls` action will produce a detailed listing of the files found.

To make it more efficient, I can add the `-type f` option to only consider regular files (not directories):
```bash
find / -type f -mtime 0 -ls
```
This will give you a list of all regular files modified in the last 24 hours, along with their permissions, ownership, and other details.
